## Steps

<figure class="story-hero"><a href="/forge-studio/media/stories/S8/01-open-the-library-and-look-at-the-shelf-f.png"><img src="/forge-studio/media/stories/S8/01-open-the-library-and-look-at-the-shelf-f.png" alt="1. Open the Library and look at the shelf forge did not write"></a></figure>

1. **Open the Library and look at the shelf forge did not write.** Four of the Library’s shelves hold parts forge ships.
2. **Press "Browse community".** One browser over four kinds — skills, hooks, MCPs and tools.
3. **Read where the twenty items actually come from.** Nine sources are declared and four of them contribute nothing.
4. **Refresh the registry against those sources.** forge crawls nothing on its own — a refresh happens exactly when an operator asks for one, and this is the ask.
5. **Check what every declared source contributes — and what the ones contributing nothing say.** This is what "browse the registry" has to mean, and it has three honest endings rather than one.
6. **Read the rows the refresh wrote into the registry.** A refresh does not only report what the sources publish — it writes it.
7. **Check the source forge could read and still had nothing to offer.** The third ending, on its own chip.
8. **Check that no row is still a hand-curated seed.** Every row currently reads "seed — never verified", which is the truth and is exactly the problem.
9. **Take the first door in — press "+ Add item" to install by URL.** The registry is a declared list, and this is how the operator declares something into it.
10. **Give forge nothing but the upstream URL and what to call it.** Star counts and last-checked dates are not on this form on purpose — they are facts a fetch establishes, not claims an operator types.
11. **Install the thing that URL names.** This is §3’s second door, and it was a wall until ruling 477 built it.
12. **Go back to the browser.** Back to the catalogue, to take the door that does end in an install.
13. **Find the one item in the registry that is executable code.** Twenty items and exactly one of them is a script.
14. **Open it and read every file in the package before trusting any of it.** Two files: the manifest that declares what it runs on and what it may touch, and the script itself.
15. **Read the security scan that runs before the install exists.** The order is the whole point: scanned before installed, not installed then scanned.
16. **Take the second door in — install it by id.** Installed, and trusted by nobody.
17. **Follow it to the page that owns the trust decision.** A hook that came from a stranger arrives in the same state as one the operator wrote by hand: on disk, described, scanned, and refused permission to run.
18. **Approve it.** One press, and a file somebody else wrote becomes something forge will execute.
19. **Open the Agents pillar.** A library part is inert until something composes it.
20. **Find the installed hook in the palette an agent composes from.** This is where S8 ends and where a community install becomes real: not when the bytes land, and not when the operator approves them, but when the thing shows up in the bin an agent is built out of.
